thread:
emma_cs: FYI customer AcmePayments reports a sudden increase in incorrect merchant-name outputs after our optimizer rollout this morning. They say examples that were fine yesterday now truncate or hallucinate company names. :frowning_face:

sam_support: Do we have customer request ids or example prompts? Which model + quant profile did they hit?

emma_cs: They called out model redwood-13b-v2 (rolled to fp8-profile-2026-03-16). Customer provided this minimal repro: 
```json
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-13b-v2\",
  \"quant_profile\": \"fp8-profile-2026-03-16\",
  \"prompt\": \"List the merchant name for transaction id 0x7f3: 'merchant:'\",
  \"temperature\": 0.0
}
```
Response they saw: "Merchant: Azura LLC" (wrong, expected "Azura Coffee Co.")
Request id: r-43f9b2a1, time: 2026-03-16T09:12:01Z

jordan_eng-ml: Thanks. A few quick checks: 1) confirm temperature/sampling; 2) check tokenization boundary changes after quantization (rare but possible if we accidentally changed preprocessors); 3) eval on known prompt-set with deterministic decode (temp=0, top_k=1).

lina_eng-runtime: I pulled the request logs with r-43f9b2a1, kernel selection shows fp8 kernels on node gpu-prod-7, batch size 1, kv-cache enabled. Latency normal (~45ms). No obvious error in runtime. I can re-run the exact request against the previous quant profile (fp8-profile-2026-03-10) and the float16 baseline.

sam_support: Customer says regression appears only for a subset of prompts that reference short tokens like 'Co.' and punctuation endings. Could be quantization trimming or tokenization mismatch.

emma_cs: Customer also attached a few more examples, all deterministic decodes. They've paused traffic to prod model and requested rollback if we can't reproduce. They marked as "business impacting" and asked for ETA.

ops_bot: Created ticket INC-2026-451 for "fp8 profile regression - merchant name drift" and assigned to eng-ml. Link: https://tickets.internal/INC-2026-451

jordan_eng-ml: I'll run a quick A/B now against: (a) redwood-13b-v2 + fp8-profile-2026-03-16 (b) redwood-13b-v2 + fp8-profile-2026-03-10 (c) redwood-13b-v2 + fp16-baseline. Will post diffs.

jordan_eng-ml: (after tests) Early results: deterministic outputs show that the new profile changes quant scale on embedding matrix in layer 7 causing off-by-one token preference for suffixes. Sample diff for prompt above: 
- fp16-baseline -> "Azura Coffee Co."
- fp8-2026-03-10 -> "Azura Coffee Co."
- fp8-2026-03-16 -> "Azura LLC"
So this looks like a small logit shift at the final token.

lina_eng-runtime: We should check whether the compiler introduced asymmetric quantization for final linear that shifts logits. Also confirm whether kernel micro-batching changed accumulation order (floating point assoc).

sam_support: Customer asked if rolling back is possible. Emma — what's the rollback process for a hosted customer?

emma_cs: For hosted API we can pin them to the older profile or route their traffic to fp16 baseline. If they want immediate mitigation we can create a per-customer route to fp8-profile-2026-03-10. Need approval from eng-ml for risk.

jordan_eng-ml: Mitigation: route AcmePayments to fp8-profile-2026-03-10 (no model change). Longer-term: revert the quant scaling change in profile-2026-03-16 and add regression tests on the merchant-name prompt set. I'll prepare a quick PR and rollback hotfix.

lina_eng-runtime: Devops note: routing change is low-risk (config only) but will bump infra counters for dedicated slots. I'll preflight the config change.

emma_cs: I told customer we can route them to previous profile immediately and will follow up with details + timeline. They're asking for RCA and whether other customers might be affected.

jordan_eng-ml: We should scan production request logs for other customers hitting this profile in last 24h and run the merchant-name prompt-set automatically to estimate impact. I'll run the scan and post counts.

ops_bot: Scan result: 17 unique customers used fp8-profile-2026-03-16 in last 24h; 4 customers had requests matching our merchant-name prompt fingerprints.

sam_support: Copying customer_acme (they're in the thread) — can you confirm you want immediate routing to previous profile?

customer_acme: Yes please, we need immediate rollback. This is blocking our payments reconciliation. ETA important.

emma_cs: Ok doing routing request now. Lina — can you apply route?

lina_eng-runtime: Routing change applied to customer AcmePayments at 2026-03-16T10:02:40Z. Verified sample requests now return expected merchant strings (matching fp16 baseline).

emma_cs: Customer confirmed outputs look correct now. They've unpaused traffic but want formal RCA and a regression safeguard.

jordan_eng-ml: RCA draft: quant scale update in fp8-profile-2026-03-16 introduced asymmetric scaling on final linear which shifted logits for short-token suffixes. Root cause: an optimization that reduced activation dynamic range without per-channel calibration on final layer. Fix: revert scaling change and add per-channel calibration + unit tests on a curated prompt set (merchant-name, dates, small tokens).

sam_support: Action items: 1) eng-ml PR to revert + tests (owner: jordan, due: 2026-03-18) 2) eng-runtime add a preflight check for quant profile rollouts that runs high-risk prompt-set (owner: lina, due: 2026-03-20) 3) CS notify customers who hit profile-2026-03-16 (owner: emma, due: 2026-03-17).

emma_cs: I'll send the customer-facing summary and link INC-2026-451. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

ops_bot: INC-2026-451 updated: mitigation applied (routing rollback), RCA in progress, severity: P2, sla breach avoided.

jordan_eng-ml: I'll also add a note to the quant docs about per-channel calibration and add a small automated diff check that flags >0.5 token-prob shift at final step for deterministic prompts.

lina_eng-runtime: Closing loop: I'll run nightly jobs to recompute profile diffs and post to #eng-ml-summary channel.

emma_cs: Customer response: "Thanks, outputs look correct now. Please confirm long-term fix and when the profile will be safe to re-roll."

jordan_eng-ml: Will follow up in INC-2026-451 with PR link and expected timeline.
